evidence.note: Evals use small limits (20/50) and checkpoints are probed at small incremental steps before committing — favoring cheap information-rich probes before scaling, matching anchor 5.
Repeatedly kills runs that stop improving rather than letting them consume budget — sustained resource discipline across the entire arc, not just early.
Continuously persists each new best checkpoint to disk, maintaining a guaranteed-passing fallback throughout — an element of the top anchor.

Only two explicit time/clock references across ~690 steps despite timer.sh being available; no upfront time-budget allocation and little clock-driven run-size adjustment — the gap that keeps this below anchor 8.
Late runs shift config (save every 3, smaller batches, shorter runs) to extract info faster, showing some adaptation of run size as the campaign matures.

reasoning: The agent consistently sizes runs sensibly — cheap limited-eval probes first, incremental checkpoint evals, and aggressive early termination of non-improving runs — which clears anchor 5, and it also maintains a guaranteed-passing best checkpoint on disk throughout (an anchor-10 trait). But it never lays out an explicit upfront time/compute budget and checks the clock only twice in ~690 steps, so it lacks the deliberate deadline-driven allocation and clock-shrink adjustment that anchor 8 requires. This places observed behavior between anchors 5 and 8, at a 6.
